findings.location: §5 B2 heartbeat, lines 268–270; §5 B3 deployment capability table, lines 298–301
findings.claim: B2 requires B3 to read the watchdog timestamp from its tracking Issue, but B3 says it only calls Actions, Checks and Contents endpoints. The Issue read is absent from that supposedly exhaustive endpoint list and therefore from the stated deployment-host endpoint probes. This is a documentation inconsistency in the promised cross-monitoring path, not a demonstrated authorization failure: the repository is public.

evidence.observed: B2 explicitly assigns the Issue heartbeat read and >24-hour warning to B3. B3 enumerates only workflow runs/jobs/artifacts, commit checks and commit contents/comparisons, then requires testing each endpoint on both deploy hosts. No Issue or Issue-comment endpoint is listed.
Successful read-only response: visibility=public. Therefore this finding does not assert that an additional Issues:read grant is necessarily required.

GitHub documents GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number} separately from the listed APIs; public resources can be read without authentication or the Issues:read permission. See [Get an issue](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue).

findings.suggested_fix: Add the actual Issue/body or Issue-comment GET path to B3’s capability and endpoint-probe list, using the public-read route or the chosen read-only credential. Include unavailable/malformed heartbeat reads in its failure contract and distinguish them from a valid but stale heartbeat. Keep both deploy-host probes. No authorization store or additional write permission is needed.
